postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:34 — `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` followed by `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)` never writes `title`, so a source entry whose title changes while its body does not permanently leaves the imported Discourse topic title stale (confidence: 100; severity: P2).

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the import method in app/models/topic_embed.rb, when updating an existing embed (lines 30-37), the code only checks if content_sha1 changed and then calls revisor.revise! with the new contents. However, it never updates the topic title. The PostRevisor.revise! method takes (user, new_raw, opts) - it only updates the post body, not the topic title. So if a source article's title changes but the body content_sha1 remains the same, the title won't be updated. Even if the body changes, the revise! call doesn't include any title update logic. This is a real bug where title changes in the source are never propagated to the Discourse topic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` followed by `rss.items.each` materializes and processes every item from an unbounded remote feed in one worker, so a large feed exhausts the worker's memory/time budget and blocks all subsequent embed imports (confidence: 100; severity: P2).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows poll_feed.rb parsing an RSS feed with `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterating over `rss.items.each` without any limit. This is a real concern - if the feed URL points to a very large RSS feed, all items would be loaded into memory and processed sequentially. However, the severity is debatable since RSS feeds are typically bounded by the feed provider, and this is a scheduled job that runs hourly. The finding correctly identifies that there's no pagination or limit on items processed, which could cause issues with unusually large feeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4 — `t.integer :topic_id, null: false` and `t.integer :post_id, null: false` create unenforced references, so deletion or a failed external write leaves an orphan whose URL lookup returns a nonexistent topic rather than allowing a clean re-import (confidence: 75; severity: P2).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the migration creates topic_id and post_id columns without foreign key constraints. This is a valid architectural concern - without FK constraints, if a topic or post is deleted, the TopicEmbed record could reference non-existent records. However, this is not strictly a bug since Rails applications commonly handle referential integrity at the application level rather than database level. The concern about orphaned records affecting re-import is speculative but reasonable. This is a legitimate design/architecture concern rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:21 — `Topic.transaction do` encloses `post = creator.create` before the unique `TopicEmbed.create!`, so concurrent imports can roll back the post/topic on the uniqueness conflict after PostCreator has already published/enqueued work for it, leaving consumers to operate on records that no longer exist (confidence: 75; severity: P2).

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition in the code. Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 19-27, the code wraps PostCreator.create and TopicEmbed.create! in a Topic.transaction. If two concurrent imports for the same URL occur, both could create posts, but only one TopicEmbed.create! would succeed due to the unique index on embed_url (shown in the migration). The failing transaction would rollback, but PostCreator.create may have already triggered side effects (jobs, notifications, etc.) that operate on the now-rolled-back post/topic. This is a legitimate concurrency bug in the transaction design.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:15 — P1, confidence 100: `poll_feed if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?` omits the sibling `embeddable_host` gate that `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` enforces, so an enabled feed imports topics even when no host has been authorized for embedding; the related embedding gates are `embeddable_host`, `feed_polling_enabled`, `feed_polling_url`, and `embed_by_username`.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that poll_feed.rb checks feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url.present?, and embed_by_username.present? but does NOT check embeddable_host. Looking at TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, it checks 'SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host'. However, this is a design consideration rather than a bug - the feed polling is a separate feature from the embedding retrieval. The feed polling imports content from an RSS feed URL (feed_polling_url), while embeddable_host controls which external sites can embed Discourse comments. These are related but distinct features. The finding raises a valid architectural concern about consistency between these two import paths, but it's not necessarily a bug since feed polling could intentionally work independently of the embedding host restriction. This is an important design/scope consideration for the reviewer to evaluate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` drops and recreates an already-present topic_embeds table whenever this migration is rerun, permanently deleting every imported-topic mapping instead of failing safely (confidence: 100, severity: P1).

adjudication.rationale: The finding misunderstands how Rails migrations work. The `force: true` option in `create_table` only affects the migration when it runs - it will drop the table if it exists and recreate it. However, Rails migrations are designed to run only once per database. The migration system tracks which migrations have been applied in the schema_migrations table, so this migration will not be 'rerun' in normal operation. The `force: true` is commonly used to ensure clean table creation during initial migration runs or development resets. This is not a bug that would cause data loss in production - migrations don't get re-executed on deployed databases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `create_table :top_topics, force: true` makes the previously shipped migration destructive on re-run, dropping the populated top_topics table and erasing all cached topic rankings before recreating it (confidence: 100, severity: P1).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb was modified to add 'force: true' to the create_table call. The 'force: true' option in Rails migrations drops the table if it exists before creating it. If this migration was previously shipped without 'force: true' and users already have data in the top_topics table, re-running migrations (e.g., during db:migrate:redo or in certain deployment scenarios) would drop and recreate the table, losing all existing data. This is a real data loss risk for a previously deployed migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read,` raises `Errno::ENOENT` for every direct embed retrieval because this code path never loads `open-uri`; [confidence: 100] [severity: P1].

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that `open-uri` is never loaded for the `import_remote` method in `topic_embed.rb`. However, looking at the diff, `open-uri` is required in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` at line 7 (`require 'open-uri'`). While this require is in a different file, Ruby's `open` method with URLs works because `open-uri` extends `Kernel.open`. The `poll_feed.rb` job would load `open-uri` when it runs. Additionally, the `import_remote` method could be called from `topic_retriever.rb` which calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. The finding assumes `open-uri` is never loaded, but this depends on the execution path and Rails autoloading. The claim of 100% confidence that it 'never loads open-uri' is incorrect - the require exists in the codebase in `poll_feed.rb`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:49 — `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` followed by `return if user.blank?` completes the retrieval job without importing whenever the configured username has no matching user, so `EmbedController#best` returns an auto-reloading loading frame forever with no failure signal (confidence 100, P1).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue in the diff. In lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 48-52, the fetch_http method does `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then `return if user.blank?`. If the configured embed_by_username doesn't match any user, the method silently returns without importing anything. Combined with EmbedController#best (lines 8-17 in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), when topic_id is nil, it enqueues the RetrieveTopic job and renders 'loading'. The loading.html.erb view (lines 6-11) has a setTimeout that reloads the page after 30 seconds. If the user is misconfigured, the job completes without creating a topic, and the page will keep reloading forever with no error indication. This is a legitimate bug - silent failure with no feedback to administrators about the misconfiguration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read,` reads an unbounded remote response with no maximum size, so an embeddable host that continuously streams an article holds a retrieval worker and grows its heap until the worker pool is exhausted (confidence 100, P1).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48: `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` which uses `open(url).read` to fetch remote content. This reads the entire response into memory with no size limit. A malicious or misconfigured embeddable host could stream an infinitely large response, causing memory exhaustion and worker pool starvation. This is a real security/availability vulnerability in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — P1 (confidence 100): The unrelated `create_table :top_topics, force: true` change expands an embed-URL-handling task into destructive top-topics migration behavior, so replaying this task's deployment drops existing top-topics data without any stated requirement authorizing that scope.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misinterprets the diff. The change from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|` is in a migration file (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb). Migrations run once and are tracked - they don't re-run on deployment. The `force: true` option only matters if the migration is run when the table already exists, which would only happen in development/testing scenarios or if migrations are being re-run manually. This is not a 'destructive' change in normal deployment - it's a minor migration adjustment that has no impact on production data during normal deployment workflows. The finding incorrectly claims this is related to 'embed-URL-handling task' scope expansion, but this is simply a separate file that was modified (possibly for whitespace or to fix a development issue).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — [confidence:100][severity:P1] `creator = PostCreator.new(user, title: title, raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` stores RSS and remote-page content as unsanitized raw HTML, so a source containing `<script>` executes on the Discourse origin for every visitor who views the imported post (stored XSS).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that TopicEmbed.import() creates posts with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], and in app/models/post.rb the cook method returns raw content directly when cook_method is :raw_html (line 131-132: 'return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]'). The content comes from external RSS feeds (poll_feed.rb) or remote pages via ruby-readability (import_remote method). While ruby-readability does filter to specific tags, it allows 'a' tags with 'href' attributes, and the RSS content uses CGI.unescapeHTML which could allow script injection. The content is then rendered with 'raw post.cooked' in the view (best.html.erb line 17), bypassing Rails' HTML escaping. This creates a stored XSS vulnerability where malicious content from external sources executes in users' browsers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26; lib/topic_retriever.rb:15; app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — [confidence:100][severity:P1] `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`, and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read,` trust a spoofable Referer and only the initial hostname, so an attacker invokes an allowed-host redirect or DNS rebinding to make the server fetch internal services (SSRF).

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real SSRF vulnerability in the new code. The diff shows: 1) embed_controller.rb:26 only checks if the referer's host matches embeddable_host, but Referer headers can be spoofed. 2) topic_retriever.rb:15 only validates the initial URL's host matches embeddable_host. 3) topic_embed.rb:48 uses `open(url).read` which follows redirects. An attacker could provide a URL on the allowed host that redirects to internal services, or use DNS rebinding where the hostname initially resolves to an allowed IP but later resolves to an internal IP. The code doesn't validate the final destination after redirects, making SSRF possible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:39 — The update test asserts only `post.cooked.should =~ /new contents/` and never verifies `app/models/topic_embed.rb:37`'s `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`, so a stale fingerprint passes the suite and causes the same feed item to be revised on every poll (confidence: 100; severity: P2).
